note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Burning/painful urination for a few days.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Pain started a few days ago; described as stinging on urination.
  - Mild lower abdominal/crampy tummy pain.
  - Blood in urine earlier today; urine described as having an unusual smell.
  - No fever reported.
- ENT symptoms:
  - None reported.
- Distribution of swelling (facial/tacial) or throat symptoms:
  - None applicable.
- Past medical history and treatments:
  - History of IBS.
- Allergies:
  - Clindamycin allergy (causes swelling).
- Current medications:
  - Over-the-counter bicarbonate used a few days ago; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Sexual health/social context:
  - Sexually active with a regular partner; uses condoms.
  - Not smoking; drinks alcohol on weekends.
  - Lives in a flat near college; student.
- Pregnancy/menstrual status:
  - Last period ~3 weeks ago; possibility of pregnancy discussed.
  - Pregnancy test advised if symptoms do not improve.
- Other relevant history:
  - Last STD screen: not performed previously.
  - Bowel function generally normal; no diarrhea or vomiting.
- Accompaniment/supervision:
  - Not specified.

Objective:
- Physical exam findings:
  - Not recorded.
- Observable ENT/oropharyngeal findings:
  - None stated.
- Airway/breathing status:
  - Not stated.
- Other observations:
  - Not stated.
- Vital signs:
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with patient:
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Primary impression:
  - Suspected simple urinary tract infection (lower UTI/bladder infection) based on dysuria with mild lower abdominal pain and absence of fever.
- Supporting details from history:
  - Burning on urination for several days; brief hematuria earlier today; no back pain or systemic symptoms.
- Conflicts:
  - None noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Antibiotic course planned: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim; "one tablet, twice a day, for three days" (drug choice not specified).
  - Advise increased fluid intake; cranberry juice recommended.
- Patient/caregiver instructions:
  - If not better by the end of this week, contact/return to see the clinician: “If you're still not better, by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me.”
  - Consider pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy if symptoms persist.
  - Avoid sexual intercourse if possible while symptoms are present; continue barrier contraception.
  - Monitor for red flags: high temperatures, back pain, feeling unwell; contact clinician if they occur.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Worsening symptoms or fever/back pain suggesting possible kidney involvement; instructions to call back.
- Follow-up:
  - Review symptoms after completing 3-day antibiotic course; if persistent, follow-up with clinician.
  - No COVID-19 vaccine considerations discussed.
- Other notes:
  - Urine testing (e.g., urinalysis) not performed/reported in transcript.
